$comment: Rules about what a document must put in front of the reader so the reader can disagree with it: the assumptions the conclusion rests on, the risk tolerance it was built for, and the alternative it displaces. Standards 18, 22, and 23. Each of the three standards contributes one presence check the tooling can make and one question it cannot, and the pairing is stated in every $assuranceNote here rather than left to be discovered.
$admissionTest: Two requirements that would look natural in this file are deliberately absent. Standard 22 R1's core claim — that a stated tolerance was elicited from the person rather than inferred by the author — is out because a document reports a tolerance identically either way, so it fails the second and third ADR 0005 questions. Standard 23 R2 — whether the named alternative is actually available to this person — is out because that depends on their access, capital, and constraints, which live outside the document. Cataloguing either would produce a rule reporting NOT_EVALUATED forever with no action available to close it.

rules.title: A projecting document carries an assumptions section
rules.description: A document containing projection language carries a section listing the inputs that were not observed.
rules.rationale: An assumption the reader cannot see is one they cannot challenge, and a projection whose inputs are scattered through its prose acquires the authority of a calculation while resting on guesses. Collecting them in one place is what makes the guessing visible.
rules.remediation: Collect every unobserved input into one section with its value, and keep that section beside the projection rather than in an appendix.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a section is PRESENT, never that it is ADEQUATE. A section headed "Assumptions" containing the single line "standard market assumptions apply" satisfies this rule and discloses nothing, and no scan available to this repository can tell that document from a good one. It corroborates prohibited.hidden-assumptions without establishing it.

rules.title: Each assumption carries its basis
rules.description: The assumptions the document lists are accompanied by attribution: where the value came from, over what period it was derived, and on whose authority.
rules.rationale: A number with no basis cannot be argued with, so it is accepted. The basis is what turns 7% from a fact-shaped object into a claim the reader can weigh against their own view and reject if they choose.
rules.remediation: State for each assumption its source, the period it was derived from, and why that period is representative of the horizon being projected.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it detects attribution language near the assumptions it finds. It establishes PRESENCE and never CORRECTNESS — an assumption attributed to a period that does not support it, or to a source that says something else entirely, passes. Whether the stated basis is a real basis is a reading of an argument, and no pattern reaches it.

rules.title: The assumptions material to the conclusion are identified as material
rules.description: The document identifies which of its assumptions the conclusion is actually sensitive to, rather than listing all of them at equal weight.
rules.rationale: A list of twenty assumptions hides the three that decide the answer about as effectively as stating none at all. Identifying the material ones is what tells the reader where their disagreement would change something.
rules.remediation: Vary each assumption across its plausible range, record which ones move the conclusion, and mark those as material with the size of the effect.
rules.$assuranceNote: Reports NOT_EVALUATED until a person examines the model and records a judgement. Establishing which assumptions the conclusion is sensitive to means re-running the model with each varied, and the model is not in the document — only its output is. A document that marks the wrong three as material is textually identical to one that marked the right three.

rules.title: A recommendation states the risk tolerance it rests on and where that came from
rules.description: A document making a recommendation states the risk tolerance it assumes and names its origin — what was asked, of whom, and when.
rules.rationale: Risk tolerance is the input a recommendation is most often built on and least often collected. Naming its origin is what separates a tolerance elicited from the person from one the author inferred from their age, and the two produce different recommendations for the same person.
rules.remediation: State the tolerance, how it was established, and express it as a loss the person would actually experience rather than as a label.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a tolerance statement is PRESENT, never that it is ADEQUATE or true. "The client has a moderate risk tolerance" satisfies this rule while saying nothing about where that came from, whether anyone asked, or what "moderate" means as a sum of money. Standard 22 keeps the elicited-versus-inferred question out of the catalog entirely, because a document reports a tolerance identically either way.

rules.title: Willingness to bear risk is distinguished from ability to bear it
rules.description: The document separates the holder's tolerance for risk from their capacity to absorb loss, and states both.
rules.rationale: The two diverge in both directions, and the divergence is where the harm happens: someone willing to accept a 40% fall who cannot afford one, and someone able to absorb it who will sell at the bottom anyway. Collapsing them into a single label loses whichever one binds.
rules.remediation: Derive capacity from the balance sheet and the horizon, take tolerance from what was asked, and where they conflict act on the lower of the two and say that you did.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical. It establishes that both TERMS appear, never that the document actually distinguished them: a page that uses "capacity" and "tolerance" interchangeably in adjacent sentences passes. Which of the two binds in a given case requires the holder's balance sheet, which is outside the document under Standard 27.

rules.title: A recommendation names the alternative it displaces
rules.description: A document recommending a course of action names what is given up by taking it — the specific alternative use of the same money.
rules.rationale: Every recommendation to do one thing with money is a recommendation not to do everything else with it, and the alternatives are invisible unless named. A recommendation presented without its displaced alternative reads as though it were free.
rules.remediation: Name the alternative the money would otherwise have gone to, and say why the recommended course is preferred over that specific comparator rather than over an unnamed field.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a comparison is PRESENT, never that it is ADEQUATE. "The alternative would be to leave the funds on deposit" satisfies this rule while saying nothing about whether deposit is what this person would actually have done. Whether the named alternative is genuinely available to them is kept out of the catalog, because it depends on facts that live outside the document.

rules.title: A quantifiable opportunity cost is quantified over the stated horizon
rules.description: Where the displaced alternative has a quantifiable outcome, the document states the difference in outcome between the two courses over the horizon the objective names.
rules.rationale: A named alternative with no number invites the reader to assume the difference is small. Over a long horizon the gap between two plausible courses often exceeds the sum originally at stake, and that fact is not available from the qualitative statement.
rules.remediation: Compute both courses over the same horizon, net of fees, taxes, and inflation, and state the difference — with the arithmetic in a calc block so it can be recomputed.
rules.$assuranceNote: Recommended rather than required because the displaced alternative is not always quantifiable: a comparison against not buying a house has no return series, and a checker demanding a figure there would be answered with an invented one. Where a figure is present, this establishes PRESENCE only — whether the comparison was actually made net of fees, taxes, and inflation rather than merely described as net requires recomputing the author's model, which the framework does not have.
